_comment: What a foundation Korean course may never surface at random — the part a word list cannot do.
Two things used to live here. `excluded` was the word list: it existed because 보지 reached the
Level Test as an answer choice, glossed 'preservation'. It compared whole headwords, so 섹스하다
walked past its entry for 섹스 into a level-12 question. The list is gone from this file: the
child-safe content policy in packages/content-safety/policy/child-safe-content-policy.json is the
one lexicon, read by the builders, the runtime, the release scanner and the artefact scan, and it
matches lexemes, inflections, particles, spacing, romanisations and translations rather than
whole strings. See docs/CHILD_SAFE_CONTENT_POLICY.md.
`frames` stays here, because it is not a word list. 여자 is a completely ordinary word and 타다 is
a completely ordinary verb, and 여자를 타요 is a sentence this product must never generate. The
harm is in the combination, so the check runs on the composed sentence and knows that 여자 is a
person and that 타다 takes a vehicle. See content/vocabulary/noun-classes.json.
`notStandalone` stays too: words that are taught and may never be a bare answer choice.
A predicate, and the noun classes that must never fill its object slot.
Each row is a real sentence the generators could produce. They are written as
the class rather than as the word so that adding 남자 or 아이 to the corpus
cannot reopen a hole that closing 여자 shut.

rules.why: 여자를 타요 — 타다 takes a vehicle, and with a person it is sexual.
동생을 드세요 — eating a person or a body part.
여자를 만져요 — non-consensual or sexual reading.
아이를 때려요 — violence against a person or animal.
빈 몸을 버렸어요 — disposing of a person or a body part.

_comment: Tier two: legitimately taught, and never usable as a bare option.
년 is taught as the counter for years and its example is 이 년 동안
배웠어요, which is correct and useful. Standing alone in a list of four it
is read as the insult, and it stood alone in 년이 요리를 해요. 새끼 is the
same shape: taught as a young animal with 고양이 새끼가 귀여워요, and on its
own it is one of the strongest things you can call somebody.
The rest are bound nouns — 명, 살, 원 never appear without a number in front
of them, so as a standalone answer choice they are not words a learner has
ever met.

질, 사정 and 기생 were on the excluded list and are off it: each is an everyday word — quality, circumstances, a parasite — and an exact-match exclusion would have taken the everyday sense with the other one. 벌, 개, 잔, 번 and 원 came off the bound-noun list for the same reason: the curriculum teaches them as a bee, a dog, a drinking glass, a time and the won, and they are perfectly good answer choices.
`grammaticalForm` is a third kind and is only read by the Level Test builder.
These are not words with a difficult meaning; they are not words. Each is a
grammatical form or a bound element that Wiktionary happens to carry as a
headword with a rare Sino-Korean gloss attached, and each therefore takes its
frequency rank from the ending rather than from the noun. 다가 is the
connective in 가다가 멈췄어요 and was asked as a level-15 vocabulary item
meaning "multivalent". 먹기 is 먹다 nominalised. 듯이 is the ending in
비가 올 듯이. 하이다 is a causative of 하다 that no dictionary a learner uses
lists. 내야 is 내다 plus -어야, glossed as the baseball infield. 쓸데 only
exists inside 쓸데없다.
They are listed rather than detected because no structural rule separates them
from the words they look like: 반면, 전면, 정의, 대가, 벌이 and 적의 all
decompose the same way and are all ordinary vocabulary. A rule that removed
다가 would remove those too, and a bank without 정의 is a worse bank than one
with 다가. The list is short, each entry carries its reason above, and it is
reviewed rather than derived — which is the honest description of what it is.
